import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1008

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1008](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1008)
- [CFS14b] Conlon, D. and Fox, J. and Sudakov, B., *Large subgraphs without complete bipartite
  graphs*. arXiv:1401.6711 (2014).
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos1008

/--
Does every graph with $m$ edges contain a subgraph with $\gg m^{2/3}$ edges which contains
no $C_4$?

This problem was first solved in the affirmative by Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS14b]. A simple
proof is given by Hunter in the comments.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1008.lean"]
theorem erdos_1008 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ H ≤ G, (cycleGraph 4).Free H ∧
        c * (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Originally asked by Bollobás and Erdős in 'a colloquium on graph theory at Tihany' with $m^{2/3}$
replaced by $m^{3/4}$. Folkman showed this is false with the counterexample $K_{n,n^2}$, which has
$n^3$ edges, and yet every subgraph with $>n^2+\binom{n}{2}$ edges contains a $C_4$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1008.variants.three_quarters : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ H ≤ G, (cycleGraph 4).Free H ∧
        c * (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Folkman's counterexample $K_{n,n^2}$, which has $n^3$ edges, and yet every subgraph with
$>n^2+\binom{n}{2}$ edges contains a $C_4$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1008.variants.folkman (n : ℕ) :
    ((completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) (Fin (n ^ 2))).edgeSet.ncard = n ^ 3) ∧
      ∀ H ≤ completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) (Fin (n ^ 2)),
        n ^ 2 + n.choose 2 < H.edgeSet.ncard → cycleGraph 4 ⊑ H := by
  sorry

/--
In [Er71] Erdős revises the conjecture to $m^{2/3}$, and notes $\gg m^{1/2}$ is trivial.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1008.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ H ≤ G, (cycleGraph 4).Free H ∧
        c * (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1008

findings.description: The docstring says the problem was “first solved in the affirmative by Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS14b].” The cited 1971 paper already credits Szemerédi with the same bound in a note added in proof. This is a historical attribution slip; the Lean theorem, answer(True), and research solved category are correct.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis (1971), p. 97, Problem 1, footnote: “Note added in proof: Szemerédi proved cn^{2/3}.” https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-25.pdf . CFS (2014), Theorem 2.1, subsequently gives the more general K_{r,r}-free bound, specializing to this result at r = 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove “first,” or credit Szemerédi as reported in the 1971 note and describe CFS14b as providing a later proof/generalization. No theorem or status change is needed.

reformulations.difference: The witness H ≤ G has the same vertex type as G, whereas the source allows arbitrary subgraphs, including vertex deletions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Extend an arbitrary subgraph by adding the omitted vertices as isolated vertices. This preserves its edge count and C4-freeness, since every vertex of C4 has a neighbor. Conversely, a spanning subgraph is an ordinary subgraph. Proved the equivalence, including the uniform constant quantifiers, in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

reformulations.difference: The negated uniform-bound property uses same-vertex-type subgraphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Adding isolated vertices preserves edge count and C4-freeness, so the positive existence properties are equivalent for exponent 3/4; consequently their negations are equivalent as well. The positive-property equivalence was proved for an arbitrary real exponent.

reformulations.difference: The universal containment assertion ranges over spanning subgraphs of the specified complete bipartite graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Adding omitted vertices as isolated vertices preserves both edge count and the presence or absence of C4. Thus the universal threshold assertion is equivalent to one over arbitrary subgraphs. Proved this equivalence for an arbitrary host graph and threshold.

reformulations.difference: The square-root lower bound is formulated using same-vertex-type subgraphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same isolated-vertex extension preserves the edge count and C4-freeness. The parameterized Lean equivalence applies with exponent 1/2.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalizations were found in the four theorem statements. Checked quantifier scope, uniform positive constants, answer polarity, ordinary rather than induced containment, finite edge cardinalities, and zero/small inputs. Lean computations exhaustively checked all 256 edge subgraphs of K_{2,4}; the largest C4-free ones have 5 edges, matching Folkman's strict threshold. Also proved the complete-bipartite edge-count formula and zero-edge cases. The cited external proof compiled successfully, and a bridge to the exact main statement was proved; both have only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as axioms. The erdosproblems.com problem page and forum returned Cloudflare 403 responses despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so comparison relied on the cited primary papers directly; the Hunter-comment reference was not independently checked.
